A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GUI-agent survey, with reliably matchable text, tables, and figures. The complete 80-page v6 and 85-page v8 support comparison; neither contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v6 synthesizes cited research and provides illustrative GUI workflows. It reports no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or empirical data-analysis results.

after.justification: v8 remains a literature survey. Added performance statements concerning MultiUI and UI-TARS are attributed to cited work, rather than experiments conducted for this survey.

M1.justification: The architecture, workflow, and component explanations in Section 5 are retained. Added descriptions of Operator, UI-TARS, and other systems concern existing external methods; neither version proposes an original algorithm that is revised here.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation using its own dataset or task suite. Added entries such as MultiUI and ScreenSpot-Pro expand the resources surveyed, rather than experimental coverage exercised by this work.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed method against baselines. New framework catalogue entries and summaries of comparisons from cited papers do not introduce a baseline experiment conducted by the survey.

E3.justification: Sections 9.1-9.3 retain the evaluation metrics, measurement approaches, and platform taxonomy. New benchmark descriptions document external resources; they do not introduce or revise an experimental protocol used by this work.

E4.justification: The illustrative workflow, reflection, and GUI-testing examples are retained. Neither version reports original ablations or robustness studies, and the added literature summaries do not constitute new supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: No repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval, or statistical-testing practice is introduced or revised. Added dataset and task counts are resource descriptions, rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v8 newly reports MultiUI's cited 48% gain on VisualWebBench and 19.1% increase in Mind2Web element accuracy in Section 7.2. Section 8.6 also adds the finding that UI-TARS outperforms GPT-4o and Claude. These are additional secondary result statements, not same-setting performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: The MDP and reinforcement-learning explanation in Section 5.7.5 and metric descriptions in Section 9.1 are retained. The additions introduce no new formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's eight research questions, and conclusion retain the same contribution: a comprehensive practical survey and research roadmap for LLM-powered GUI agents. The additional literature does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: v8 adds specific mechanism explanations, including how AutoDroid-V2's scripts reduce repeated model queries and how BrowserGym's standardized observation and action spaces address fragmented evaluation. The general limitations and future roadmap in Section 11 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New catalogue entries provide additional technical metadata and resource links, including UI-TARS's 7B/72B configurations, six million GUI tutorials, and repository in Table 22. These expand documentation of surveyed resources; the survey's own repository and searchable-page disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The literature review expands across grounding, frameworks, datasets, models, benchmarks, and industry systems. Additions include Iris, ScreenSpot-Pro, OS-Genesis, Operator, UI-TARS, and GTArena, while Table 2 adds several related GUI-agent surveys. This is a broad substantive expansion beyond citation renumbering.

P1.justification: The twelve-section organization and most existing prose are retained. Changes include localized model and benchmark paragraphs, revised table introductions, and renaming Section 5.7.1 from GUI Parsing to GUI Grounding.

P2.justification: Framework, dataset, model, and benchmark tables are extensively regrouped into platform-specific tables. A dedicated grounding Table 6 is added, incorporating OmniParser from v6 Table 16. Figure 3 gains Claude Computer Use, Operator, and UI-TARS; most other figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The dedicated grounding summary and platform-specific tables make resources easier to locate and compare, while the Operator and UI-TARS additions update the survey's account of the field. Awkward new wording and an overflowing link in Table 6 reduce polish. With the central synthesis and limitations unchanged, the net improvement is useful but limited.
